data.gender_notes: Azmira is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Azmira is a Sanskrit name derived from the Goddess Apsara, symbolizing love, beauty, and grace. In Hindu mythology, the Apsaras are celestial beings responsible for performing arts, music, and dance for the gods. The name Azmira carries the meaning “Goddess of Love and Beauty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Azmira usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of love and beauty and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Azmira total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Azmira was an ancient Hindu goddess of beauty and love. She was identified with the goddess Apsara Riddhi, who was the embodiment of riches and prosperity. Azmira is mentioned in various ancient Indian texts, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

Another reference to Azmira can be found in the Jain scriptures, where she is described as the goddess of love and desire. She is said to have tempted the Jain ascetics with her beauty and charms, but ultimately failed to distract them from their spiritual pursuits.
